source.title: Large Stepsizes Accelerate Gradient Descent for Regularized Logistic Regression
source.authors: Jing-Feng Wu; Pierre Marion; Peter L. Bartlett

record.file_problem: Full text provided; no apparent truncation or corruption.
record.tranche_reason: The paper's own results concern convex, ℓ2-regularized logistic regression on linearly separable data. It does not test the listed versions about non-convex neural networks, benchmark classification error, teacher-student minima, normalization, or squared-loss wide networks. Deep-learning edge-of-stability work appears as cited prior work.
record.gate_note: The paper reports theoretical convergence and divergence results for logistic regression and a two-dimensional simulation. Its discussion of neural networks and edge-of-stability findings cites other studies; those cited results are not extracted as rows.
record.test_reason: The study proves convergence results and simulates convex, regularized logistic regression with linear predictors. None of V1–V6 covers this system. Its discussion of neural-network edge-of-stability results cites prior work; extensions to neural networks are proposed, not demonstrated.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. More precisely, the authors establish acceleration bounds for separable ℓ2-regularized logistic regression, matching Nesterov's rate under sufficiently small regularization, extend the benefit to population-risk upper bounds under statistical uncertainty, and characterize the local convergence threshold under additional assumptions. Global convergence near that threshold is proved only in one dimension and remains open generally.
record.recipe_differences: Constant-stepsize GD on convex, ℓ2-regularized logistic regression; the listed versions concern non-convex neural networks and benchmark classification error or other neural-network-specific settings.
record.method_sensitivity: Convergence depends on regularization, stepsize, and data assumptions; the paper gives distinct bounds for small versus general regularization and a critical threshold under the support-vectors condition.

fits_no_version.finding: Large constant stepsizes give accelerated objective-convergence bounds for regularized logistic regression on bounded, separable data.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For separable ℓ2-regularized logistic regression, suitably large constant stepsizes improve GD step-complexity bounds from O(ln(1/ε)/λ) to O(ln(1/ε)/√λ) under small regularization, or O(ln(1/ε)/λ^(2/3)) under general regularization, treating margin dependence as constant.

fits_no_version.finding: Under the support-vectors condition, the local convergence and almost-everywhere nonconvergence thresholds have scale 1/(λ ln(1/λ)).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For finite-dimensional separable regularized logistic regression under the stated support-vectors condition, sufficiently small constant multiples of this threshold permit local convergence; sufficiently large multiples prevent convergence for almost every initialization.

fits_no_version.finding: The two-point simulation reports convergence through η = 32 and initial sharpness oscillations around 2/η, followed by a stable phase.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Regularized linear logistic regression can exhibit transient edge-of-stability dynamics and faster convergence with larger constant stepsizes in the reported toy setting.

record.peer_reviewed: Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2025), 39th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems
record.problems: The theoretical results rely on bounded separable data and, for the threshold result, an additional support-vectors condition. The simulation is a two-point, two-dimensional logistic-regression example; no neural-network experiment or benchmark classification-error result is reported. The stated bounds use constants whose values are not specified.

rows.subject: GD for ℓ2-regularized logistic regression
rows.operation_detail: Constant-stepsize GD from w0 = 0 on linearly separable data; theoretical convergence bound under Theorem 1 conditions.
rows.measure: Steps to reach ε objective error after phase transition
rows.value: With the largest allowed stepsize and λ ≲ γ²/n²: O(ln(1/ε)/√λ) steps
rows.note: The bound is theoretical for regularized logistic regression, not neural-network classification.
rows.check: No applicable claim version. Corollary 2 bounds total steps, including the phase transition, rather than only subsequent steps. The simplified O(ln(1/ε)/√λ) rate treats γ as constant; the explicit bound is O(max{1/(γ√λ), n/γ²} ln(1/ε)).

rows.check: No applicable claim version. Clarify that divergence means failure to converge to the minimum: objective error exceeds some positive ε infinitely often. The theorem does not establish that iterates or objective values grow without bound.
